look_here_first: Nonlocal A. incanum comparison: 5 style/stigma branches and about 5 mature fruit segments, often dark-centered reflexed corolla. FNA does not place the species in Texas; a Hays identification merits comparison with A. fruticosum. Do not rely on staminal-column hair alone; A. fruticosum floras disagree.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small yellow or pink flowers often dark-centered

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Calyx 3–5 mm; corolla reflexed, yellow or pink with dark red center, petals 4–6 mm; staminal column pubescent; style 5-branched.

key_traits.label: Fruit seed
key_traits.text: Schizocarp cask-shaped, not medially constricted, 7–9 × 6 mm; mericarp apex acute/apiculate, tomentulose; 3 seeds per mericarp, seeds ~2 mm.

lookalikes.differences: The expected Texas look-alike A. fruticosum usually has plain yellow flowers and 6–9 style branches.

source_credit: Existing Hays Botany species record and scientific source notes; original full record retained in assigned family staging branch
